newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill to amend bond rules for Indian tribes.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill to amend bond rules for Indian tribes.

text.p: California lawmakers will debate later Wednesday a bill clearing the way for Indian tribes to participate in controversial Marks-Roos bond transactions.
The state's so-called Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act allows many types of government agencies to form joint powers authorities to finance capital projects.

Last year, state Treasurer Matt Fong called for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the state's Attorney General to investigate several California Marks-Roos bond transactions that involved Indian tribes.

In those deals, the Indian tribes were represented to be the "local agencies" on whose behalf the bonds were issued, Fong said. But according to the state treasurer, Indian tribes are not eligible to participate in those types of transactions.
Fong said these bond offerings violated the "letter and spirit" of state law, and he urged the SEC and attorney general to investigate the deals.
Assembly Bill 229, by Republican Assemblyman Jim Battin, would amend the Marks-Roos bond act to expand the definition of local agency to include federally recognized Indian tribes.
The Assembly Committee on Local Government is expected to consider the measure at its meeting late Wednesday.
No formal opposition has been filed thus far to the bill, but committee staff said critics could emerge at the hearing.
